scope: Public MIT, arXiv and SSRN sources relevant to Phoenix structured products.

sources.topic: reduced models for basket options under BS/Heston
Chebyshev Greeks; memory worst-of autocall example
stochastic volatility and correlations in worst-of autocallables

sources.use: dataset discovery/taxonomy; outcome evidence not assumed

sources.topic: conditional analytic Monte Carlo for autocallables

theory_methodology: MIT OCW 15.450 lectures on stochastic volatility, Heston, simulation, barrier options, and control variates: Highly relevant for theoretical foundation and methodological improvements in Phoenix's pricing and simulation frameworks.

MIT DSpace paper on reduced models for basket options under Black-Scholes/Heston: Relevant for methodological advancements in reduced-form models, particularly for basket options, which may inform Phoenix's handling of multi-asset structures.

arXiv 2106.12431 Chebyshev Greeks with a memory worst-of autocall example: Relevant for methodological improvements in sensitivity analysis (Greeks) and handling path-dependent features in autocallables.

SSRN 3228065 on stochastic volatility/correlations in equity worst-of autocallables: Relevant for methodological extensions to incorporate stochastic volatility and correlation dynamics in worst-of autocallables.
SSRN 4214697 pricing autocallables under local-stochastic volatility: Relevant for methodological improvements in pricing autocallables under more realistic local-stochastic volatility models.
SSRN 1125725 conditional analytic Monte Carlo for autocallables: Relevant for methodological advancements in efficient Monte Carlo simulation techniques for autocallables.
verified_market_evidence: SSRN 2411789 collecting US autocall issuance data and contractual properties: Useful for out-of-sample (OOS) validation and training data to assess Phoenix's performance against real-world market data.

useful_for_engine: MIT OCW 15.450 lectures: Directly applicable for improving simulation engines, control variates, and barrier option handling in Phoenix.
arXiv 2106.12431: Useful for enhancing sensitivity analysis (Greeks) and path-dependent feature handling in autocallables.
SSRN 1125725: Applicable for improving Monte Carlo simulation efficiency in Phoenix's engine.
useful_for_data: SSRN 2411789: Provides real-world issuance data and contractual properties, useful for training and validating Phoenix's data-driven components.
review.next_experiment: Implement stochastic volatility (Heston) and local-stochastic volatility models in Phoenix's simulation engine, incorporating control variates and Chebyshev-based Greeks for path-dependent autocallables. Validate against real-world issuance data from SSRN 2411789.

committee_review.baseline: Phoenix canonical Monte Carlo and payoff engine with incomplete OOS evidence
committee_review.target: Use public theory as challenger/methodology input without converting papers into market labels
committee_review.next_experiment: Select one variance-reduction method and one stochastic-volatility/correlation challenger for offline comparison against canonical engine.
committee_review.final_devin_validation: Sources classified; no paper result treated as realized evidence and no production logic changed.
